name: renewal-generate
description: Flow 6. The T-100 per-entity timer (contract artefact 5 concern "renewal-generate", name renewal-generate:<policyId>). Publisher-initiated, so it works by HANDOVER (plan 1.3): it mints ONE broker-side quote_config record, pre-filled from the expiring term's highest submission version, and never writes it again — after creation the answers are the broker's. It then writes a submission_config v1 stamped origin: "publisher-renewal" (1.3: "these are the answers the broker attested" is not true of a clone), whose quote_id is the handover quote's record id, and calls underwriting-evaluate on it so the renewal is rated and ruled against the CURRENT tables. Plan 5.3's open question is decided here in favour of routing new-unanswered-questions to referral: the renewal carries the current product_version, and a question added since the original bind is unanswered, which wave 4's A-11 already forces to REFER rather than a silent ACCEPT. Answers are copied by PATTERN (gen_/clm_/itcl01_/ahcl/cpl_/gp01_), so a new question is carried across with no flow change. Idempotent on the presence of a publisher-renewal submission in folder <policyId>; a caller passing regenerate:true mints a NEW record at revision Q-REN-<policy_number>-R<n> and supersedes the old through its outcome (1.3 part 3), which closes spec 4.4's Q-REN uniqueness defect by construction. Timer payload: {policy_id, concern, quote_id, regenerate?}.

static.note_handover: The broker-side quote is created ONCE. Regeneration mints a new record and supersedes the old through its outcome; it never overwrites the broker's answers, which is the collision plan 1.3 exists to prevent.
static.note_regeneration: Spec 4.6.3's "automatically invalidates and re-generates" stays TASK-DRIVEN, matching wave 6's flow 8: flow 8 raises the invalidation task and a human calls this flow with regenerate:true. Automatic regeneration would have this flow overwrite a broker-side record it is forbidden to touch.
